decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 1.5% to 1.75%. The vote was 8-0.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in March indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a moderate rate.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in January indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activi…”

changes.quote: Job gains have been strong, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has stayed low.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Job gains have been strong in recent months, and the unemployment rate has stayed low.”

changes.quote: Recent data suggest that growth of household spending moderated from its strong fourth-quarter pace, while business fixed investment continued to grow strongly.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Recent data suggest that growth rates of household spending and business fixed investment have moderated from their strong fourth-quarter readings.”

changes.quote: On a 12-month basis, both overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy have moved close to 2 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “On a 12-month basis, both overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy have continued to run below 2 percent.”

changes.quote: Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Market-based measures of inflation compensation have increased in recent months but remain low; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are …”

changes.quote: The economic outlook has strengthened in recent months.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee expects that economic conditions will evolve in a manner that will warrant further gradual increases in the federal funds rate; the federal funds rate is likely to remain, for some time, below levels that are expected to prevail in the longer run.
The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting strong labor market conditions and a sustained return to 2 percent inflation.

This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 13.16% APR costs about $54.83 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.97% and moved 0 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.47% would not change.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4%, and employers added an average of 252k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.3% over the past year (March 2018); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.9%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.3% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -1 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.72%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.38% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 66%, cut 0%, hike 34%.

citations.detail: In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent.
